items.headline: Essex teens born from 2009 will never be legally sold cigarettes
items.summary: A new law starts on 1 January. Anyone born in 2009 or later can never be sold tobacco, even as an adult.
body: In 30 days, the rules on selling tobacco change for good. From Friday 1 January, no shop in Essex will be allowed to sell tobacco to anyone born on or after 1 January 2009. That means everyone in the county who is 17 or younger now can never legally be sold a cigarette, however old they get.

The law creates what ministers call a smoke-free generation. Each year the age of sale effectively rises by one year, so tobacco is phased out a generation at a time. Those born on New Year's Day 2009 turn 18 on the day the law starts, becoming the first adults in Britain who can never legally buy cigarettes.

The change comes from the Tobacco and Vapes Act 2026, which became law on 29 April. It covers cigarettes, rolling tobacco, cigars, shisha and heated tobacco, as well as herbal smoking products and cigarette papers. It does not cover vapes, which stay on sale to over-18s.
It will also be an offence for anyone aged 18 or over to buy tobacco for someone born in 2009 or later. Shops must put up an age-of-sale notice at every till where tobacco is sold.
The cut-off date never moves. Someone born in 2009 will still be refused at 40.
## What it means for Essex shops

Trading standards teams enforce the law: Essex County Council's across most of the county, and Southend City Council's and Thurrock Council's in their own areas. Since 29 October, officers have been able to hand out on-the-spot fines rather than going straight to court. For most offences the fine is £200, cut to £100 if paid within 14 days.
## How many people in Essex smoke

Smoking is already falling. Government figures published in October show 9.5% of adults in England smoked in 2025, the first time the figure has dropped below 10%. [As The Seax reported](/story/o-essex-smoking-record-low/) at the time, smoking in the Essex County Council area also fell to its lowest level on record.

The picture still varies a lot across Essex. The Office for National Statistics publishes local rates as five-year averages, because survey samples in each district are small. Analysis of those figures by The Seax shows that for 2021 to 2025, five Essex council areas were above the England average of 10.9%.

Basildon and Thurrock had the highest rates, both 13.4%, followed by Tendring on 13.3%, Harlow on 13% and Uttlesford on 11.9%. Rochford had the lowest rate in Essex, at 4.8%, followed by Maldon on 7.1% and Brentwood on 7.3%.
The figures come with wide margins. In Harlow, for example, the true rate could lie anywhere between 8% and 17.9%.

Let's Be Clear, the East of England's tobacco control programme, is marking the 30 days to go. It brings together councils across the region, and Thurrock Council announced in February that it had joined. The programme says 8.9% of adults in the East of England still smoke, and more than 6,500 people in the region die from smoking every year.

Its programme lead, Hannah Clougherty, said the government, councils, shops and enforcement teams must make sure the law is understood and enforced from day one. "This isn't about waiting for another generation to become addicted and then trying to help them quit," she said. "It's about preventing the next generation from becoming addicted in the first place."

Anyone born before 2009 can still buy tobacco, and free help to quit is on offer across Essex. The Essex Wellbeing Service, which covers the county outside Southend and Thurrock, has helped 14,280 people stop smoking since 2022, according to Essex County Council. Southend and Thurrock run their own free services, with up to 12 weeks of support and free quit aids such as nicotine replacement products or a vape kit.
